how_read: Each page was read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py (its page-render call). Each quote is the page's text as the fetcher printed it. Where a page's own sentences disagree, the note follows the section about Mario Kart 64 and the 'conflicts' list says so.
conflicts: Fake Item Box page: its opening paragraph says Fake Item Boxes cannot block incoming Green or Red Shells, but its Mario Kart 64 section and the Red Shell page say they can block shells in this game. The note follows the Mario Kart 64 section and the Red Shell page.

lines.line: Summary: A Banana is a peel you drop on the track, and a kart that runs over it spins out. The Banana Bunch puts five Bananas in a trail behind your kart.

quoted: Drops a banana peel, making a racer spin out when it is run over.
Summons five Bananas behind the racer.

lines.line: Uses: The Bunch lets you throw each Banana one by one whenever you like, and the Bananas in the trail also block incoming items from hitting you. You can drop only one banana at a time.

quoted: The player may throw each Banana one-by-one whenever they please, and the Bananas also block incoming items from hitting the player.
The player can drop only one banana peel at a time

lines.line: Tips: Held behind your kart, a Banana guards against homing Red Shells and, less well, Green Shells.

quoted: It can also be held behind the kart as a defensive countermeasure against homing Red Shells and, to a lesser extent, Green Shells.

sections.name: Green Shell and Triple Green Shells

lines.line: Summary: A Green Shell is thrown in a straight line at another racer, and the racer it hits flips over several times. Triple Green Shells put three shells in a ring around your kart.

quoted: A shell that can be thrown in a straight line at another racer. If it hits, the racer flips multiple times.
Summons three Green Shells into a barrier that surrounds the racer that used the item.

lines.line: Uses: A Green Shell bounces off walls a number of times until it hits a target or is destroyed, and holding the stick backwards fires it backwards. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against items and projectiles, and the ring can also ram other karts.

quoted: Green Shells can ricochet off walls a number of times until they hit a target or are destroyed.
when the player holds the analog stick backwards, the shell now gets fired backwards instead of dropped
the shells can be used to guard against items and projectiles, as well as turning the kart into a battering ram against other karts
The player may throw each Green Shell one-by-one whenever they please, and can also use the Green Shells to block incoming items.

lines.line: Tips: The triple shells cannot be fired backwards and are slightly harder to aim because they keep rotating around the kart. Computer racers do not get Green Shells in this game.

quoted: Unlike the single Green Shell, however, these shells cannot be fired backwards and are slightly harder to aim as they are constantly rotating around the kart.
Computer-controlled opponents do not receive this item in the game

sections.name: Red Shell and Triple Red Shells

lines.line: Summary: A Red Shell locks on to the racer directly in front of you. Triple Red Shells put three Red Shells in a ring around your kart.

quoted: Red Shells automatically lock on to the racer directly in front of the item user.
Summons three Red Shells into a barrier that surrounds the racer that used the item.

lines.line: Uses: A Red Shell can only be thrown forward, but it follows the road to hit its target, and it is destroyed if it hits a wall. With the triple, you throw the shells one at a time or keep them as a shield against incoming items.

quoted: Red Shells can be thrown only forward in this game, but they now follow the road to hit the target racer. However, Red Shells get destroyed if they hit any walls or the like.
The player may throw each Red Shell one-by-one whenever they please, and can also use the Red Shells to block incoming items.

lines.line: Tips: In this game only, a Fake Item Box can block an incoming Red Shell. A Banana held behind your kart also guards against Red Shells.

quoted: In this game only, Fake Item Boxes can be used to block incoming Red Shells.
It can also be held behind the kart as a defensive countermeasure against homing Red Shells

lines.line: Summary: The Spiny Shell is the rarest item. It travels along the ground with a siren sound and flings the racer in the lead into the air.

quoted: It is the rarest item
Once fired, the Spiny Shell travels forward, making a siren sound
It targets the player character in the lead, flinging them into the air upon contact

lines.line: Uses: It can only be fired forward, never backwards, and it can travel over gaps and jumps. Any other racer in its way is flung into the air too. If you fire it from first place, it turns around and hits you.

quoted: cannot be thrown backwards
The Spiny Shell can travel over gaps and jumps.
but this also occurs to other racers in the way
If the player character uses the Spiny Shell in first place, the item turns around to hit them.

lines.line: Tips: If the shell hits an obstacle it is destroyed, and it is also destroyed without hurting a racer who is invincible. If the leader is invisible the shell passes through them, though it may make another lap of the course and hit them afterwards.

quoted: If the Spiny Shell hits an obstacle, it is destroyed.
If the Spiny Shell strikes an invincible racer, it gets destroyed without damaging the racer.
If the leader is invisible, it simply passes through them, though it may then simply make another lap of the course and hit them afterwards.

there are two sideways Item Boxes that will always contain a Spiny Shell, no matter the player's position. One appears underneath the hot-air balloon in Luigi Raceway, and the second atop the large rock in Koopa Troopa Beach.

lines.line: Tips: Two sideways Item Boxes, one under the hot-air balloon on Luigi Raceway and one atop the large rock on Koopa Troopa Beach, always give a Spiny Shell whatever your place.

quoted: If the Spiny Shell hits an obstacle, it is destroyed.
If the Spiny Shell strikes an invincible racer, it gets destroyed without damaging the racer.
If the leader is invisible, it simply passes through them, though it may then simply make another lap of the course and hit them afterwards.

there are two sideways Item Boxes that will always contain a Spiny Shell, no matter the player's position. One appears underneath the hot-air balloon in Luigi Raceway, and the second atop the large rock in Koopa Troopa Beach.

lines.line: Summary: A Mushroom gives you a short speed boost. Triple Mushrooms give you three boosts that you use one at a time.

quoted: Gives a racer a short speed boost.
they grant the player three consecutive speed boosts that can be used one-by-one.

lines.line: Uses: Ramming another racer while boosting from a Mushroom makes them spin out. The triple's effect wears off once the last Mushroom is used.

quoted: ramming into another racer while boosting from a Mushroom causes the opponent to spin out
The effect wears off once the last Mushroom is used.

lines.line: Tips: In Bowser's Castle, a Mushroom or a Star lets you drive through the grass of the first courtyard and cut off the first two turns.

quoted: A notable shortcut can be found at the first courtyard. The player can use Mushrooms or a Star to drive through the grass, cutting off the first two turns.

lines.line: Summary: What later games call the Golden Mushroom is the Super Mushroom here, a yellow-capped mushroom whose icon has a glow behind it.

quoted: the Super Mushroom (renamed the Golden Mushroom in later games)
the Super Mushroom appears simply as a yellow-capped mushroom, though its icon also shows a glow behind it.

lines.line: Uses: It gives you endless speed boosts for a limited time: you can boost your speed as many times as you want while it lasts.

quoted: It gives the player an endless amount of speed boosts for a limited time.
For a limited time, you can boost your speed as many times as you want.

lines.line: Tips: In the item window, look for the yellow-capped mushroom with the glow behind it.

quoted: the Super Mushroom appears simply as a yellow-capped mushroom, though its icon also shows a glow behind it.

lines.line: Summary: A Super Star makes you invincible for about ten seconds: you can drive through items, course obstacles and other racers.

quoted: 10.13 seconds for Mario Kart 64
invincible to all attacks and able to drive through items, course obstacles, and hit other drivers
Makes racers invincible, rendering them impervious to obstacles, other items, and other racers.

lines.line: Uses: You also drive about a third faster and can go off-road unhindered. A racer you hit flips over and loses the item they are holding.

quoted: The player receives a speed boost increasing their average speed by 1/3 in all games except Super Mario Kart and Mario Kart: Super Circuit
Players may also traverse off-road unhindered while under the effects of a Super Star.
Being hit by a driver using a Super Star causes the driver to flip and lose their currently held item.

lines.line: Tips: If you hit a wall hard enough that your character exclaims, the Star ends at once.

quoted: If a racer, while using a Super Star, hits a wall or the like in such a way that their character exclaims, the Super Star's effect immediately ends.
Lightning's effect can be avoided if a racer has a Mega Mushroom, Star, Boo, or Bullet Bill item activated when the bolt strikes
If the Spiny Shell strikes an invincible racer, it gets destroyed without damaging the racer.

lines.line: Tips: A Star that is running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, and a Star destroys a Spiny Shell without hurting you.

quoted: If a racer, while using a Super Star, hits a wall or the like in such a way that their character exclaims, the Super Star's effect immediately ends.
Lightning's effect can be avoided if a racer has a Mega Mushroom, Star, Boo, or Bullet Bill item activated when the bolt strikes
If the Spiny Shell strikes an invincible racer, it gets destroyed without damaging the racer.

lines.line: Summary: Lightning, called the Thunder Bolt in this game, shrinks every other racer, which slows them down and lets other karts flatten them.

quoted: The Thunder Bolt returns in Mario Kart 64
all racers except for the one that used the item shrink, slowing them down and allowing them to be run over.

lines.line: Uses: Shrunk racers cannot use Mushrooms, Super Stars or Boos from their item windows, but they keep the items they hold. Karts that are not shrunk can ram smaller ones to flatten them, and two shrunk racers who run into each other crush each other.

quoted: Racers do not lose items as a result, but shrunken racers cannot use Mushrooms, Super Stars, or Boos in their Item Windows.
Unaffected racers can ram into smaller players to flatten them and if two shrunken racers run into each other, they will both crush each other.

lines.line: Tips: A Super Star or a Boo that is already running when the bolt strikes keeps you from shrinking. While Lightning is in effect a sound like a tiny alarm plays.

quoted: Lightning's effect can be avoided if a racer has a Mega Mushroom, Star, Boo, or Bullet Bill item activated when the bolt strikes
In Mario Kart 64, Mario Kart: Super Circuit, and Mario Kart: Double Dash!!, when Lightning is used, a sound like that of a tiny alarm is heard during its effect.

lines.line: Summary: A trap that looks like a normal Item Box, but its question mark is upside down. A kart that hits one is blasted into the air.

quoted: They appear identical to regular Item Boxes with a key difference: the question mark inside is upside-down (a ¿ instead of a ?). Karts that collide with one are blasted into the air.

lines.line: Uses: Hold it behind your kart and it blocks incoming shells, as a Banana does. Unlike a Banana it cannot be tossed forward, and if you place it in midair it floats.

quoted: can be held behind a kart
Like Bananas, they can be used to block incoming shells, though unlike Bananas, they cannot be tossed forward. If placed in midair, a Fake Item floats

lines.line: Tips: Look at the question mark when you drive up to a box: the fake one's is upside down.

quoted: the question mark inside is upside-down (a ¿ instead of a ?)

lines.line: Summary: The Boo item makes you invisible and invincible for a short time while it steals an item from an opponent.

quoted: When used, a Boo makes the user both invisible and invincible temporarily as it selects an opponent to steal an item from, unless the racers have no items

lines.line: Uses: While it lasts you can pass through items, course obstacles and other racers. Computer racers use Boos too, but their Boos do not steal items.

quoted: A player character affected by a Boo can pass any items, course obstacles, and racers by going through them.
The CPUs also use Boos, but they do not steal items.

lines.line: Tips: A Boo that is already running when Lightning strikes keeps you from shrinking, but once you are shrunk you cannot use a Boo from your item window.

quoted: Lightning's effect can be avoided if a racer has a Mega Mushroom, Star, Boo, or Bullet Bill item activated when the bolt strikes
shrunken racers cannot use Mushrooms, Super Stars, or Boos in their Item Windows.

lines.line: Summary: Blue stone blocks in Bowser's Castle that try to flatten racers who drive under them. Some slam down from the air, and some slide from side to side on the ground.

quoted: They appear in Bowser's Castle and try to flatten any player that races beneath them.
being blue cubes that lack spikes
There are also some Thwomps that move from one side to the other, trying to bump players on the ground

lines.line: Weak points: They are obstacles in the course, not something you fight. Run into one and you spin out, but if one steps on you, you are squished flat. A Super Star makes you impervious to obstacles.

quoted: Thwomps serve as obstacles in the course.
if you run into one, you will spin out. Should you be stepped by one, you'll find yourself squished flat as a pancake.
Makes racers invincible, rendering them impervious to obstacles, other items, and other racers.

lines.line: Tips: The first corridor after the courtyard has four Thwomps that move around in the air before falling. In the next corridor a pair wait at the start, try to follow you, then fall and return, and the row at the end takes turns falling: one Thwomp in 50cc, two in 100cc and three in 150cc.

quoted: Once racers leave the courtyard they enter a wide corridor with four Thwomps; these Thwomps will move around in the air before falling onto the track.
A pair will wait at the beginning of the corridor and then attempt to follow racers before falling and then returning to the beginning of the corridor.
the number of Thwomps in the row depends on the engine class (one for 50cc, two for 100cc, and three for 150cc), and they will always take turns falling.
enter a room with two more Thwomps; these ones are always at ground level and move from side to side.
there is an imprisoned slightly larger Thwomp tinted green with yellow teeth due to the vertex shading approximating the yellow lighting, which shakes and laughs if racers go near it.

lines.line: Tips: Two Thwomps in a later room stay at ground level and slide from side to side. The slightly larger green Thwomp locked up at the end of the first corridor shakes and laughs when you go near.

quoted: Once racers leave the courtyard they enter a wide corridor with four Thwomps; these Thwomps will move around in the air before falling onto the track.
A pair will wait at the beginning of the corridor and then attempt to follow racers before falling and then returning to the beginning of the corridor.
the number of Thwomps in the row depends on the engine class (one for 50cc, two for 100cc, and three for 150cc), and they will always take turns falling.
enter a room with two more Thwomps; these ones are always at ground level and move from side to side.
there is an imprisoned slightly larger Thwomp tinted green with yellow teeth due to the vertex shading approximating the yellow lighting, which shakes and laughs if racers go near it.

lines.line: Summary: Two trains run clockwise around Kalimari Desert all the time and cross the track. A kart that drives into a train is launched upward.

quoted: There are two trains that move clockwise around the track constantly, often getting in the way of racers and launching them upward if driven into.

lines.line: Weak points: Wait for the train to pass: the booklet says to time it so the locomotive does not block you, and to stop for a moment if it is crossing in front of you. Computer racers always stop at a crossing when the train is there. You can also drive through the gap between the coaches to get past.

quoted: The trick is to time it so that the steam locomotive that crosses the course won't block you. If the train is crossing in front of you, you should temporarily stop.
CPU drivers always stop at a train track if the train is present.
One can drive through the gap between the coaches of the train to bypass it.

lines.line: Tips: The train's length depends on the number of players: one coal tender and five passenger cars when you play alone, an engine, a tender and one passenger car in two-player VS, and no tender or passenger cars in two-player Grand Prix or three- and four-player VS.

quoted: single-player features one coal tender and five passenger cars; two-player VS mode has shorter trains, an engine, a coal tender, and a passenger car each; two-player Grand Prix and both three- and four-player VS mode have no coal tender or passenger cars.
The train track can be driven around in a loop, but it is not counted as a lap if driven the entire way around and only puts players who take it behind.

lines.line: Tips: The train track can be driven round as a loop, but going the whole way round does not count as a lap and only puts you behind.

quoted: single-player features one coal tender and five passenger cars; two-player VS mode has shorter trains, an engine, a coal tender, and a passenger car each; two-player Grand Prix and both three- and four-player VS mode have no coal tender or passenger cars.
The train track can be driven around in a loop, but it is not counted as a lap if driven the entire way around and only puts players who take it behind.

lines.line: Summary: A giant Yoshi's egg spins around in a large circular area near the end of Yoshi Valley and flattens any racer in its path.

quoted: A giant Yoshi's egg that spins around, flattening any racer in its path.
leads to a large circular area with a rotating, hazardous Giant Egg.

lines.line: Weak points: The wiki describes no way to stop it; it is part of the course. A rope bridge leads you past the circular area and out of the valley to the finish line.

quoted: A rope bridge leads them past the area and takes them out of the valley to the grassy area they began in, where they cross the finish line.

lines.line: Tips: Once all the routes have joined, the winding road to the egg has few railings.

quoted: Once all the routes have converged, racers take a winding road with few railings that leads to a large circular area
Afterward, it takes a steep 270° left turn full of porcupines before a drop that merges it with route 2
Porcupines walk from side to side, spinning out a racer who collides with them.

lines.line: Tips: Route 5 has a steep 270 degree left turn full of porcupines, which walk from side to side and spin out any racer who hits them.

quoted: Once all the routes have converged, racers take a winding road with few railings that leads to a large circular area
Afterward, it takes a steep 270° left turn full of porcupines before a drop that merges it with route 2
Porcupines walk from side to side, spinning out a racer who collides with them.

lines.line: Summary: Chainless Chomps are lodged in the middle of Rainbow Road, and a racer who collides with one is launched into the air.

quoted: Chainless Chomps are embedded into the track, chomping around at random. If a racer collides with one, they are launched into the air.
several Chomps can be found lodged in the middle of the track.

lines.line: Weak points: The wiki describes no way to stop them; they are part of the course. They travel the course in reverse and slide in a zigzag pattern.

quoted: They continuously travel the course in reverse and slide in a zigzag pattern.

lines.line: Tips: In this game Rainbow Road has rails along the whole track.

quoted: it has rails throughout the entire track.
It is the longest race course in Mario Kart 64, at 2,000 meters, and it requires about two minutes per lap.

lines.line: Tips: It is the longest course in the game, 2,000 meters, and takes about two minutes a lap.

quoted: it has rails throughout the entire track.
It is the longest race course in Mario Kart 64, at 2,000 meters, and it requires about two minutes per lap.

lines.line: Summary: Cars, tanker trucks, box trucks and school buses drive along Toad's Turnpike, and a racer who collides with one is knocked into the air.

quoted: these include white cars, turquoise tanker trucks, red box trucks (which can carry three different cargo types), and yellow school buses.
If a racer collides with one, they are knocked into the air.

lines.line: Weak points: The vehicles follow the same route as you, except in Extra, where they drive against you at the speed they have in 150cc. The engine class sets their speed: traffic is slow in 50cc and quite fast in 150cc.

quoted: The vehicles travel follow the same route as players, except in Extra mode, where they drive against players at the same speed as in 150cc. The engine class also affects how fast the vehicles move; traffic moves slowly in 50cc, but it is quite fast in 150cc.

lines.line: Tips: The larger vehicles go slowly and can block you, especially where the road is two lanes and vehicles travel side by side, which makes it hard to steer between them.

quoted: the larger vehicles go slowly through the road, sometimes blocking the player (especially where the roadway is two lanes, and vehicles often travel side-by-side, making it difficult to steer between them).
At the beginning of the right U-turn, the roadway merges into two lanes, and remains this way until racers pass the finish line.

lines.line: Tips: The road merges into two lanes at the start of the right U-turn and stays that way to the finish line.

quoted: the larger vehicles go slowly through the road, sometimes blocking the player (especially where the roadway is two lanes, and vehicles often travel side-by-side, making it difficult to steer between them).
At the beginning of the right U-turn, the roadway merges into two lanes, and remains this way until racers pass the finish line.
